comments.author: MaxA
comments.text:
I'm pasting this bit of my agent's research as a standalone piece because it's a convoluted setup that needs to be fully understood for a good forecast (mine is coming up a bit later) on this question and 45374, and the agent's work is probably better than a human could do in a reasonable amount of time.

\----

#### Who's involved

* **Good Ventures** is the foundation of billionaire Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna. It supplies most of the money below, and that money is available to spend now.
* **Coefficient Giving** decides where Good Ventures' money (and some other donors' money) goes, through grants to charities.
* **GiveWell** researches global health charities, recommends which ones to fund, and raises money from donors to fund them.
* **New AI-wealth donors** are the founders and employees of Anthropic, who have pledged to give away much of their wealth. Their wealth is mostly company shares they can't sell yet because they are locked until about mid-2027.

#### What happened

In December 2025, Coefficient promised \$175M for 2026 to charities GiveWell recommends. In July 2026 it raised that to **\$1 billion for 2026**.

Its stated reason: it expects much more donor money to arrive in a few years, mainly from AI wealth. Donors who can spend now (Good Ventures) should therefore spend early, and donors whose money is still locked up will carry more of the load later. Coefficient calls it "a one-off surge rather than a new steady state".

So 2026 is an unusually big year, and it was made big on purpose because more money is expected later.

#### The two questions count the same \$1B differently

Both questions compare later years to 2026, so what counts in 2026 matters most.

**45386 (GiveWell's "funds raised" each year).** GiveWell counts a Coefficient promise in the year the promise is for, regardless of when the money is spent. When Coefficient promised \$300M over 2023–2025, GiveWell recorded exactly \$100M in each of those three years. So the entire \$1B goes into GiveWell's 2026 figure. (GiveWell's year runs February to January, so its "2026" ends January 2027.)

**45374 (Coefficient's public list of grants).** Here each grant is counted in the year it is approved. GiveWell has to find specific charities and programs to put the \$1B into, and it can only approve so many grants before December 31. It expects to approve about \$1B of grants in total in 2026, and part of that is paid from its own donors' money. My estimate is that about \$600M of Coefficient's \$1B gets approved in 2026 and the rest in early 2027.

|                                   | Where the \$1B lands                       |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| GiveWell's funds raised (45386)   | All \$1B in 2026                           |
| Coefficient's grants list (45374) | About \$600M in 2026, about \$400M in 2027 |

#### Why GiveWell's 2027 could come in below 2026

Rough numbers for GiveWell:

* **2026:** about \$1.75B, made of Coefficient's \$1B plus about \$750M from all other donors.
* **2027:** Coefficient probably gives much less, around \$200M. There are two reasons:
  * It deliberately spent ahead of schedule in 2026.
  * GiveWell will still have unspent money from the \$1B to use in 2027.
* **The new AI donors arrive late.** Most insiders' shares only become sellable around mid-2027. After that, donors often park money in their own giving accounts first and hand it out gradually.

So for 2027 simply to match 2026, new donors must cover the roughly \$800M drop in Coefficient money. They might (a few very large gifts would do it), but it isn't the most likely outcome. 2028 is when the new money should show up in size.

One more effect cuts against the new money. Coefficient only funds GiveWell's charities while they are at least as good a use of money as its other options. If new donors fill GiveWell's best opportunities, the remaining ones are less effective, and Coefficient gives less. So new donor money partly **replaces** Coefficient's money instead of adding to it.

#### Why Coefficient's own total (45374) looks better

* **The surge is a smaller share of Coefficient's total.** Coefficient is also growing its AI safety grants to over \$1B in 2026, plus other areas, so its 2026 total is about \$2.5B. The drop in GiveWell money matters proportionally less.
* **Part of the \$1B counts in 2027,** because of the approval timing above, which helps the 2027 comparison.
* **Good Ventures also holds Anthropic shares,** estimated at \$16–50B at the expected IPO valuation. When those become sellable, Coefficient's own budget can grow, mostly in 2028.

comments.author: Zaldath
comments.text: It's worth noting how the math here actually works. I initially assumed that 100% would mean the baseline (2026) level, but actually that would be 0% - and 100% means doubling it instead, while 200% means tripling it! So there should still be a bit of weight on values below 100% (a slowed down growth scenario - but still not a reduction), especially for 2027, and no special focus around 100% (since it means doubling rather than staying flat in this case).

comments.author: Zaldath
comments.text:
Assuming the Anthropic IPO occurs around November 2026 and the employee lockup periods expire gradually during 2027, there could be a large amount of new funding coming for GiveWell in the next year or so, since a large portion of that sudden income (especially for Anthropic co-founders) is likely going to EA-related charities like GiveWell and Coefficient Giving:

[https://www.transformernews.ai/p/anthropic-employees-philanthropy-billions-donations-effective-altruism-coefficient-giving-ai-safety](https://www.transformernews.ai/p/anthropic-employees-philanthropy-billions-donations-effective-altruism-coefficient-giving-ai-safety)

In fact, the expected cash injection is so large - potentially even tens of billions of dollars - that even if it's split among several organizations, that's still vastly more than their regular funding levels. If GiveWell received only a smaller portion of the potential total sum, such as a couple of billion dollars, that would still 10x or so its funding for the next year or two. Besides, the total sum could be even larger - or GiveWell's share considerably greater. Even if the extra funding fails to meet expectations, it's likely to multiply GiveWell's funding for the next couple of years.

One extra complication is that Anthropic may be planning to delay its lockup periods for quite a while (although some of it would be gradually unlocked earlier on as well):

[https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/05/anthropic-lockup-periods-longer-180-day-ipo/](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/05/anthropic-lockup-periods-longer-180-day-ipo/)

If that's true, it could mean that a lot of that cash won't be available for 2027 yet, and possibly only partially in 2028 as well.

Regardless, there should be meaningful growth already in 2027, and likely explosive growth during 2028 (especially compared to 2026). Depending on how the lockup periods get set up, a large share of all that extra cash might become available only in 2029 and later, though.

With all these various uncertainties, it's difficult to estimate precise amounts yet. I'll just use somewhat tentative rough estimates for now. It should be much easier to estimate in late October / early November or so (assuming the lockup period schedule is openly released sometime soon before the IPO etc.).

(My current exact tentative medians are: 150% for 2027, >200% for 2028)
